title: MZ "Current Tileset has incomplete flag data"

posts.author: Madre_Joshua
posts.body:
I have run into a very strange issue as of very recently. I was working on my project as normal, when suddenly, I started getting this error message whenever I booted up any save file and tried to playtest the game.
The strange thing is, I have been working on my game for five hours straight and this error has only now been popping up; I've easily restarted the game over a hundred times in these hours and never did I get this error. It also started coming up even though I haven't touched any tileset related things in a while. I have no idea what might have caused it?
I googled the issue already and found someone else with the same issue; It was recommended to them they make a new project and use the "copy page" function from another tileset's page. I did exactly this, copying the overworld 1 tileset from this new project over my custom one in the project I am currently working on, but this same error still pops up whenever I start my game. Could anybody tell me what could possibly be the cause?
EDIT: Upon further experimenting, this only happens when I step onto one specific tile on one specific map and I have no clue what the issue is? I have posted the tile in question below. There is nothing unusual about this tile I can find. It uses the exact same assets from the tileset as the three tiles right above it, but it causes this strange error to pop up for seemingly no reason?

posts.author: ExCarbon
posts.body:
The "incomplete flag data" error generally means that
something
about your map’s tile configuration is invalid or out of sync with the project's tileset data, even if you haven't touched your tilesets in a while. The issue is usually that RM can't find or interpret one of the tiles passability flags
You can start by double checking the map's tileset assignment, make sure that the tileset your map is using IS indeed the one you expect. On Map Properties for the affected map make sure it's referencing the correct tileset. Often times somewhere during development we tend to duplicate/reorganize map IDs and forget to switch the map's tileset
Probably also a good idea to check the custom tileset on your database if you're using any custom images - especially in the B-E tabs. Could also very well be a dimension issue. Keep an eye out for placeholders (like blank gray boxes or something) that may appear if an image resource is missing or incorrectly assigned. Then simply make sure that your tile image has the correct dimensions and tile counts that match what RM is expecting (each TS is typically 768 by 768 for B-E, containing 16x16 tiles). If it's another somewhat weird dimension you can definitely end up with out of range tile indices without a doubt
